mcqs.q: Inflammation is best defined as:
opts: A protective local response of blood vessels to injury
mcqs.explain: Inflammation is a protective local response of blood vessels to injury, aiming to eliminate the agent and promote repair — it is not itself a disease (except in autoimmune disease).

mcqs.q: Inflammation of an organ is usually named by adding which suffix?
mcqs.explain: Inflammation is named with the suffix ~itis (appendicitis, hepatitis, stomatitis); pneumonia (lung) is an exception.

mcqs.q: Which is a cause of inflammation?
opts: Infection, trauma, immune reactions, necrosis or foreign bodies
mcqs.explain: Causes of inflammation include infections, chemical/physical agents, immune reactions (allergy), tissue necrosis and foreign bodies.

mcqs.q: The cardinal sign 'rubor' (redness) is caused by:
mcqs.explain: Rubor (redness) and calor (heat) result from vasodilation and increased blood flow (hyperaemia).

mcqs.q: The cardinal sign 'tumor' (swelling) is due to:
mcqs.explain: Tumor (swelling) is caused by inflammatory exudate leaking out due to increased vascular permeability.

mcqs.q: The five cardinal signs of acute inflammation are:
opts: Rubor, calor, tumor, dolor and functio laesa
mcqs.explain: The cardinal signs are redness (rubor), heat (calor), swelling (tumor), pain (dolor) and loss of function (functio laesa).

mcqs.q: The three events of the acute inflammatory response are:
opts: Vasodilation, increased permeability (exudate), and leukocyte migration
mcqs.explain: Acute inflammation involves change in vascular diameter (↑ flow), increased permeability (exudate), and leukocyte migration (cellular events).

mcqs.q: Vasodilation in acute inflammation is mediated by:
mcqs.explain: Vasodilation is mediated by nitric oxide and histamine, producing hyperaemia, redness and heat.

mcqs.q: Increased vascular permeability in the EARLY phase is mediated by:
mcqs.explain: Early permeability is mediated by histamine and bradykinin; the later, sustained phase is mediated by TNF and IL-1.

mcqs.q: The MAIN cell of acute inflammation is the:
mcqs.explain: Neutrophils (PMNs) are the main cells of acute inflammation; monocytes migrate to tissue and become macrophages.

mcqs.q: Rolling of leukocytes on the endothelium is mediated by:
mcqs.explain: Rolling is mediated by selectins; firm adhesion/margination is mediated by integrins.

mcqs.q: The passage of leukocytes through the vessel wall (diapedesis) involves:
mcqs.explain: Diapedesis (transmigration through the vessel wall) is mediated by CD31 (PECAM-1).

mcqs.q: Chemotaxis (directed leukocyte movement toward injury) is driven by:
mcqs.explain: Chemotaxis is the directed movement of leukocytes toward inflammation, driven by chemoattractants such as C5a, LTB-4 and interleukins.

mcqs.q: Phagocytosis is enhanced by coating the microbe with:
mcqs.explain: Opsonins (e.g. C3b) coat the microbe, enhancing its recognition and engulfment (phagocytosis) by leukocytes.

mcqs.q: Which mediator is responsible for FEVER and PAIN (and is reduced by aspirin)?
mcqs.explain: Prostaglandins cause fever, pain and vasodilation; aspirin reduces prostaglandins, giving anti-inflammatory, antipyretic and analgesic effects.

mcqs.q: Histamine, released from mast cells, mainly causes:
mcqs.explain: Histamine (and serotonin) from mast cells increase vascular permeability and cause vasodilation.

mcqs.q: Inflammatory exudate is composed of:
opts: Water, dead cells, inflammatory cells, proteins and bacteria
mcqs.explain: Exudate is fluid leaking through permeable vessels, composed of water, dead/inflammatory cells, proteins and bacteria.

mcqs.q: Pus is best defined as:
opts: Exudate rich in neutrophils and proteins
mcqs.explain: Pus is an exudate rich in (dead) neutrophils and proteins; a collection of pus walled by fibrous tissue is an abscess.

mcqs.q: A periapical (dental) abscess consists mainly of:
opts: Dead neutrophils, bacteria and necrotic debris
mcqs.explain: Abscess pus consists mainly of dead neutrophils, bacteria and necrotic debris, walled by fibrous tissue.

mcqs.q: A fibrinous exudate (high fibrin, few neutrophils) is typical of:
mcqs.explain: Fibrinous inflammation has a high-fibrin exudate; a classic example is fibrinous pericarditis.

mcqs.q: The systemic effects of acute inflammation include:
mcqs.explain: Systemically, acute inflammation produces fever and leukocytosis (raised white-cell count).

mcqs.q: The possible OUTCOMES of acute inflammation are:
opts: Resolution/healing, progression to chronic inflammation, or abscess formation
mcqs.explain: Acute inflammation can resolve (heal), progress to chronic inflammation, or form an abscess.

mcqs.q: In acute pulpitis, the severe throbbing pain is most attributable to:
mcqs.explain: Pain in acute inflammation is caused by increased tissue tension plus bradykinin and prostaglandins.

mcqs.q: The PRIMARY role of neutrophils in acute inflammation is:
mcqs.explain: The primary role of neutrophils is phagocytosis and intracellular killing of bacteria (via free radicals and lysozymes).

saqs.q: Define inflammation and list the five cardinal signs.
saqs.a: A protective local vascular response to injury. Cardinal signs: rubor (redness), calor (heat), tumor (swelling), dolor (pain), functio laesa (loss of function).

saqs.q: List the three events of acute inflammation.
saqs.a: Vasodilation (↑ blood flow), increased permeability (exudate), and leukocyte migration (cellular events).

saqs.q: List the steps of leukocyte recruitment with one mediator each.
Match these mediators to their action: histamine, prostaglandins, bradykinin.

saqs.a: Exudate = inflammatory fluid (water, cells, proteins, bacteria). Pus = exudate rich in neutrophils. Abscess = a collection of pus walled by fibrous tissue.

saqs.q: Why is aspirin an anti-inflammatory drug, and what other effects does it have?
saqs.a: It reduces prostaglandins, so it is anti-inflammatory, antipyretic (fever) and analgesic (pain).

saqs.q: What are the systemic effects and outcomes of acute inflammation?
saqs.a: Systemic: fever and leukocytosis. Outcomes: resolution/healing, chronic inflammation, or abscess.
